title: The dangers of dirty bulking (and why I don't recommend it)
summary: NH argues that dirty bulking (gaining mass on junk food) is the worst of both worlds: heavy fat gain, micronutrient deficiency, and likely less muscle than a clean bulk due to low protein. He stresses that health is everything, that dirty bulks set beginners up for failure (food addiction, inability to cut), and that patience over years beats rapid mass gain.

claims.claim: He prioritizes warning people against harmful practices over giving beneficial advice, because benefits can be learned later but damage can be permanent.
A bulk done properly, with foods that agree with you, adequate macros and micronutrients, can still be relatively healthy even though you gain fat and may stress your metabolism.
Dirty bulking is the worst of both worlds: you are in a surplus, but the mass comes from foods very high in fat, carbs and sodium and very low in micronutrients.
Nutrition is more case-by-case than exercise because of genetic differences between individuals; no single diet is best for everyone.
Deep squats are the best leg hypertrophy exercise for the vast majority of people, though not every individual.
A junk-food based diet is good for no one; nobody gets healthier on it.
Health is everything to him; having seen people suffer and die, he cannot accept lifting approaches that disregard health.
On a dirty bulk you gain lots of fat while lacking micronutrients and fiber, so organs struggle and you feel sluggish and bloated; from a physique perspective there is no point.
He rejects the idea that dirty bulking builds as much muscle as clean bulking; junk food is high in carbs and fat but low in protein, so he thinks you build less muscle.
Most dirty bulkers are skinny beginners; becoming fat does not fix the insecurity of being small, it turns a skinny guy into a skinny-fat or small fat guy.
He started lifting at about 100 lbs; the weight he gained was muscle and a lot of fat, but distributed around muscle rather than mostly fat.
People he knew dirty bulked, gained around 40 lbs and got stronger, then could not cut because they were physically addicted to fast food; most ended up quitting lifting fatter and unhealthier.
Novices are drawn to dirty bulking because it promises fast strength progress: mass moves mass, so lifts go up almost always.
Unless you plan to stay a very heavy lifter forever, mediocre lifts and a terrible body are not worth it; always question your ulterior motive for doing something.
Influential YouTubers who tell skinny young men to eat everything ignore patience, the number one quality needed to build a good body.
Instead of gaining all your mass in 8-10 months, gain it over 5 years; you will mostly put on muscle that way.
He was forced into a clean bulk by lack of resources, which he now sees as a blessing.
He says he is not genetically gifted and built his physique over about 10 years, not 3.
Higher body fat is linked to lower testosterone, which reduces muscle building, so excessive fat gain sabotages the goal of bodybuilding.
Leaning out afterwards does not fully reverse the damage of carrying excess weight on tendons, heart, liver and kidneys.
Dirty bulking is lazy, the easy way out and the path of least resistance.
